scope: Functional McKernel OS/apps and Rust/assembly migration only; no security testing.
findings: Final ordinary and checked release atomically transitions refcount 1 to 0 before profile/procfs and writer-locked thread hash removal. The original find body increments unconditionally while the hash reader is held and can acquire 0 to 1 in the remaining linked interval; the final releaser subsequently destroys the returned object. Hash chaining increments VM refcount, not a thread reference; initial count 2 alone does not show hash-owned exclusion.

Candidate concrete Rust public find_thread only uses a conditional SeqCst CAS when 0 < count < INT_MAX under the hash reader; relative to a non-forced final atomic decrement this prevents resurrection. Overflow, zero and negative counts refuse lookup; exited warning follows successful hold. Existing generic extern callback ABI and ordinary hold_thread are untouched. Scope relies on matching reader/writer lock, live thread and Process fields until writer detach and no separate force reset.

Procfs Rust find_proc_thread returns a raw list member after releasing threads reader; process_procfs_request_inner invokes hold_thread only afterward, unlike the C body which holds while locked. Final destruction can remove/free in that gap. Even locking during hold alone does not address zero-to-one resurrection.

The direct process- and thread-directed do_kill selectors traverse under process or thread locks and call unconditional hold_thread; their exited-status exclusion and all failure/unwind paths require review. The C find_thread fallback still uses the unchecked generic callback.

Legacy C clone cleanup can publish a PS_RUNNING thread then force refcount to 1; this may erase acquired references. The full28 Rust supported CLONE_VM projection documents its error edges as pre-publication, so the legacy counterexample is not automatically applicable to that projection. terminate_host also force-sets a detached-thread reference and its exclusion requires proof.
fixture_limits: Generic-c reports expanded fixture using actual candidate and both original release bodies with mock ABI and decrement, a host RwLock and a deterministic two-thread zero-before-lookup ordering. Includes PID mismatch/fallback/invalid, zero warning suppression and INT_MAX/negative. Reviewer did not rerun it. It is not a test of real MCS/IRQ providers, native behavior or unrelated acquisitions.
required_tests: Actual selected lookup and both release bodies with deterministic final-decrement-before-lookup and lookup-before-decrement, then real concurrent read/write-lock exclusion in a bounded fixture.
Zero/negative/INT_MAX, exited warning and no warning on refusal, matching pid, wildcard fallback, duplicate and absent tid, lock balancing and no destruction while a successful reference is held.
Separately exercise procfs list protection/try-hold ordering, direct kill paths, and selected force-refcount cleanup with their real bodies before whole-lifecycle claims.
